title: Light in fiber goes about 200 km per millisecond
body: Glass has a refractive index near 1.47, so signals in fiber travel at roughly two-thirds of vacuum light speed, about 200 kilometres per millisecond one way. A round trip across an ocean therefore costs tens of milliseconds no engineering can repeal. Cloud regions are placed by physics first and marketing second.
source_hint: Refractive index of silica fiber, networking texts
